title: Spread of COVID-19 Vaccine Misinformation in the Ninth Inning: Retrospective Observational Infodemic Study
screen_reason: Content analysis of a keyword-defined Twitter corpus (436 tweets on 'Hank Aaron' + 'vaccine'), manually coded for misinformation, reporting a share of items classified as vaccine misinformation with an explicit denominator (n=244, 56% of 436). Meets the CONTENT criterion.

estimates.country: Not stated; Twitter corpus was multilingual (tweets in Spanish, Turkish, Japanese, Portuguese, German, Slovenian, Dutch), event was US-based
estimates.measure_type: % of tweets in a keyword-defined event corpus manually coded as vaccine misinformation
estimates.denominator: 436 tweets returned by the Twitter Search API v1.1 for the keywords "Hank Aaron" and "vaccine", 31 Jan-6 Feb 2021 (the 'Initial Sample')
estimates.definition: Tweet coded as misinformation if it attempted to link the death of Hank Aaron with administration of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine (the other two codes being reporting/news media and public reaction).
estimates.misinfo_def: tweets "coded ... as ... misinformation, if they attempted to link the death of Hank Aaron with administration of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine"; the underlying claim being an "unfounded link between Aaron's death and the COVID-19 vaccine"
estimates.source_quote: Results: A total of 436 tweets were initially sampled from the Twitter Search Application Programming Interface. Misinformation was the most prominent content type (n=244, 56%) detected, followed by public reaction (n=122, 28%) and media reporting (n=69, 16%).
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results; the same counts appear in Results, first paragraph (p. 4)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Manual annotation by authors AC, MH and a former team member using the WHO SAGE Vaccine Hesitancy Matrix as the coding frame; "achieved a high intercoder reliability (kappa=0.83) for misinformation codes with discrepancies reviewed and reconciled by rereviewing SAGE categories with all authors".
estimates.moderator_quote: Tweets and user comments associated with the keywords "Hank Aaron" and "vaccine" were queried with the Twitter Search API from January 31, 2021, to February 6, 2021 (the week immediately following the death of Hank Aaron), hereinafter referred to as the "Initial Sample."
estimates.notes: Single-issue keyword corpus around one event, hence denom_scope=topical. The authors requested a maximum of 1000 tweets and the query returned 436, so the cap did not bind and the set is not rank-truncated (denom_selection left blank). Country coded Global: the sample was not country-restricted and included non-English tweets (<1% of corpus), although the event and the study's framing are US. 244/436 = 55.96%, consistent with the verbatim 56%.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) the 'Seeded Sample' figure that 612/779 (78.6%) of comments on misinformation-labelled tweets 'expressed positive sentiment or agreement' with that content - this is agreement/sentiment toward misinformation, not a share of items that ARE misinformation, so it is not a prevalence estimate under any construct; (b) the SAGE theme distribution among those comments (individual/group influences 65% n=508; vaccine-specific 14% n=110; contextual 12% n=93; unclassified 9% n=70) - theme categories, not falsity; (c) public reaction (n=122, 28%) and media reporting (n=69, 16%) - the non-misinformation complement categories of the same 436-tweet denominator, which are not misinformation shares; (d) 'Four users engaging with or posting misinformation were verified on Twitter' - a bare count of accounts with no denominator (fails R1/R8); (e) the 22% antivaccine-sentiment figure quoted from reference [5] in the Introduction, which is another paper's number and excluded by R8.

rob.design: Retrospective observational infoveillance study. Sampling frame: Twitter Search API v1.1 keyword query ("Hank Aaron" AND "vaccine"), 31 Jan-6 Feb 2021, max 1000 tweets requested, 436 returned; a snowballed 'Seeded Sample' of 1243 comments from 973 unique users (779 analysed) and a 'Verified Account Sample' of non-media verified accounts. Coding procedure: manual annotation by three coders into news media / public reaction / misinformation, plus WHO SAGE hesitancy coding and manual sentiment annotation; Google Translate used for the <1% non-English tweets. Reliability as reported: intercoder kappa=0.83 for misinformation codes, discrepancies reconciled by all authors. No response rate applicable (platform data). Authors flag limited generalizability of the narrow keyword set.
rob.item6_quote: The Initial Sample of tweets were manually coded by authors AC, MH, and a team member no longer with the research team as (1) reporting or news media, (2) public reaction, or (3) misinformation, if they attempted to link the death of Hank Aaron with administration of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine.
rob.item10_quote: A total of 436 tweets were returned from the Twitter Search API based on our keyword query that made up our Initial Sample of tweets collected for this study. After a first round of manual coding for misinformation content per the SAGE categories, vaccine misinformation was found to be the most prominent content type detected (n=244, 56%).
